start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-a-short-list with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"}, list \"news\", indexed_fields [\"kind\"] and items [{\"seq\": 1, \"kind\": \"a\", \"text\": \"x\"}, {\"seq\": 2, \"kind\": \"b\", \"text\": \"y\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the short list is kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-a-short-list" with store, the list's name, its indexed_fields and the whole list as it should now be.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every attempt must give the outcome the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run writes only what changed: a new or changed item, a removed one, and the head when the order or the counts changed; the same list again writes nothing.

worked_examples.title: A short news list kept, then one item added
worked_examples.ask: Keep my news list with these two items, then add a third.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the list kept in the tables short_list_head and short_list_item with their keys, made by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept_ids ["news"], refused [] and found_ids ["news"]; only item 3 and the head are written, and the counts read kind a 2, kind b 1.
